title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000034: uint64_t is absent from both CMock's standard :treat_as: map and the project's, so :memcmp_if_unknown: emits an 8-byte memcmp of a by-value scalar's address; fixing it exposed a second, genuine test defect
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft': configuration defect measured from the CMock generator source and fixed in the SIL harness configuration, with the two affected tests verified green. The same defect remains present in the shipped conf/unit/ and is NOT fixed there, because conf/ is out of scope for this work. A second test-side defect was found and fixed as a direct consequence. human approval remains 'pending'. No MISRA conformance, tool-qualification or certification claim is made.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: First record. Root cause located in the CMock type map rather than in the tests, fixed in the SIL harness configuration, and the newly-surfaced test defect recorded with its own evidence.

evidence: ROOT CAUSE, read from the CMock generator source rather than inferred. 'uint64_t' appears NOWHERE in CMock 2.7.2's standard_treat_as_map (ceedling-1.1.9/vendor/cmock/lib/cmock_config.rb:141-183), which maps uint8/uint16/uint32 and their _t spellings plus the other C scalar spellings, but contains no 64-bit unsigned entry - verified by a direct search returning zero matches. It is also absent from the shipped project's own ':treat_as:' list at conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml:362-367, which lists only uint8, uint16, uint32, int8 and bool. With neither source supplying it and ':memcmp_if_unknown: true' set at conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml:368, cmock_unityhelper_parser.rb:34 does not raise and instead falls through to line 36, returning the memory fallback. For a BY-VALUE argument that yields UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_MEMORY with the '&' argument modifier, i.e. CMock emits, for the by-value uint64_t parameter 'canSignal' of CAN_TxSetMessageDataWithSignalData (src/app/driver/can/cbs/can_helper.h:131-136): UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_MEMORY(&cmock_call_instance->Expected_canSignal, &canSignal, sizeof(uint64_t), ...). That is an 8-byte memcmp of the ADDRESS of a scalar, so it compares two stack addresses and fails whenever the value happens to differ. Confirmed verbatim in the generated mock Mockcan_helper.c:500 and :528. Symptom before the fix, identical in both affected tests: 'Memory Mismatch. Byte 0 Expected 0x00 Was 0x38:Function CAN_TxSetMessageDataWithSignalData Argument canSignal' at test_can_cbs_tx_f_debug-build-configuration.c:698 and :1757, and 'Memory Mismatch. Byte 0 Expected 0x00 Was 0x6A' at test_can_cbs_tx_f_pack-minimum-maximum-values.c:718 and :881. Note this is a configuration defect and NOT a product defect and NOT a driver bug: can_helper.h:131 correctly declares a by-value uint64_t. FIX APPLIED, in the SIL harness configuration only (docs/artifacts/.work/verification-env/sil/run.sh, which rewrites its own isolated copy of the Ceedling project file): ':treat_as:' gains 'uint64_t: UINT64' and 'uint64: UINT64'. CMock then emits UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_UINT64 and the assertion checks the VALUE, which is what the test means. A SECOND, GENUINE TEST DEFECT WAS EXPOSED BY THE FIX, and this is the substantive reason the finding matters. Once the assertion compared values instead of addresses, it failed with a real value mismatch: 'Expected 0 Was 18446744073709551416'. That second operand is 18446744073709551416 - 2^64 = -200, which is BC_TEMPERATURE_MIN_CHARGE_MSL_ddegC (src/app/application/config/battery_cell_cfg.h:124). The product passes '(int64_t)signalData' (can_cbs_tx_f_debug-build-configuration.c:874), the correct sign-extended conversion. The test passed 'temperatureMinChargeSignals[0u]', a float_t, directly into a uint64_t parameter. Measured on this host: (uint64_t)(-200.0f) is 0, while (uint64_t)(int64_t)(-200.0f) is 18446744073709551416. Converting a negative float to an unsigned type is not the same value as sign-extending it, so the test's EXPECTATION was 0 and the code under test was right. Under the broken address comparison this defect was invisible, because the comparison never looked at the value. The same shape appears in test_can_cbs_tx_f_pack-minimum-maximum-values.c, where testMinimumTemperature0 is -150.0f (line 99) and the product uses '(int64_t)signalData' (can_cbs_tx_f_pack-minimum-maximum-values.c:447). FIXED test-side by casting the signal fixtures through (int64_t) at the expectation sites, exactly as the product does: 81 sites in test_can_cbs_tx_f_debug-build-configuration.c and 4 in test_can_cbs_tx_f_pack-minimum-maximum-values.c, each carrying a comment recording why. The cast is confined to the test's own expectation arguments and changes no product behaviour. RESULT: test_can_cbs_tx_f_debug-build-configuration.c 23/23 and test_can_cbs_tx_f_pack-minimum-maximum-values.c 14/14, both previously 21/23 and 12/14.
impact: Two distinct things were wrong and only one of them was visible before. The configuration defect made four assertions compare stack addresses, which is an assertion that cannot detect a wrong value and can fail for reasons unrelated to the code - the worst kind of oracle, because it looks like coverage. Fixing it revealed a real test defect that had been hidden underneath it for as long as the configuration had been wrong: the tests encoded an expectation of 0 where the driver correctly encodes -200, because a negative float_t was implicitly converted to uint64_t instead of sign-extended. That defect is a silent under-test of a CAN signal path, and it is exactly the kind that an address comparison cannot find. The cost of the fix is bounded and was measured: the SIL harness configuration changed, no file under src/ changed, and the two affected tests went from 21/23 and 12/14 to 23/23 and 14/14 with zero regressions across the 313-test suite. The limit must be stated: the defect in conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml is NOT fixed there. Only the SIL harness's isolated copy carries the ':treat_as:' entry. A run against the shipped conf/ on Linux or Windows will still exhibit the address-comparison behaviour and will still hide the negative-float defect. That is a product-owner decision about the shipped configuration and it is recorded here as open, not closed. Passing these two tests under the SIL harness says nothing about CAN bit packing on a real bus, about signal scaling or offset, or about any other device behaviour; the harness mocks the HAL and verifies driver logic against upstream's own assertions only. No MISRA conformance, tool-qualification or certification claim is made or implied.
root_cause: Two independent defects stacked on the same four assertions. FIRST, a CMock configuration gap: uint64_t is in neither CMock's standard ':treat_as:' map nor the project's ':treat_as:' list, and ':memcmp_if_unknown: true' then converts 'CMock does not know this type' into 'compare the bytes of the argument', which for a by-value scalar means comparing the bytes of its address. CMock's generator cannot distinguish 'a pointer I was asked to dereference' from 'a scalar of a type I have no comparator for' at that point, and for the latter the address is the only thing it has. SECOND, and previously masked by the first, a test defect: the tests pass a negative float_t signal fixture directly into a uint64_t parameter, producing an expectation of 0, whereas the product sign-extends via an explicit (int64_t) cast and produces the correct two's-complement value. The first defect hid the second because the address comparison never inspected the value at all. The fix for the first is a ':treat_as:' mapping for uint64_t; that alone is not sufficient to make the tests pass, and treating it as sufficient would have left four assertions failing for a reason that has nothing to do with the configuration.
resolution: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. Resolved: the SIL harness configuration now maps uint64_t and uint64 onto Unity's UINT64 comparator, so CMock emits a value comparison for by-value 64-bit arguments instead of an address comparison; and the newly-surfaced test defect is fixed by casting the signal fixtures through (int64_t) at the expectation sites, matching the product's own conversion. Both affected tests are green: test_can_cbs_tx_f_debug-build-configuration.c 23/23 and test_can_cbs_tx_f_pack-minimum-maximum-values.c 14/14, verified by a full 313-test host sweep with zero regressions. NOT RESOLVED and recommended for the product owner: the same ':treat_as:' gap exists in the shipped conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml and was NOT modified, because conf/ is outside the scope of this work. Until it is, the shipped configuration still compares by-value 64-bit arguments by address and still conceals the negative-float conversion defect from anyone running the suite on Linux or Windows. That is recorded as an open configuration defect with a one-line fix identified and deliberately not applied. Also unchanged by this work: the 4 class-A tests that remain red for want of a correct oracle, recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000033, and the test_dp83869.c segfault, recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000035.
